title: Theo's 1% Fee Cost Him $268K 😬
description:
Nora and Theo both invest $500 a month for 40 years and get the same 7% return before fees. The only difference: Nora's index fund charges 0.05% a year, Theo's fund charges 1%. Theo says 1% is nothing... until the final totals land: $1.23 million vs $958K.

A fee that looks tiny is charged on your WHOLE balance every year, so it grows with your money. Here the gap ($268K) is bigger than all $240K Theo actually put in.

What's the expense ratio on your 401(k) or IRA funds? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Assumptions: $500/month each for 40 years, 7% a year before fees, fees taken as a lower yearly return, compounded monthly, held constant, no taxes or inflation. Theo's 1% fee is an assumption; source for 0.05%: ICI, Trends in the Expenses and Fees of Funds, 2025 (index equity mutual funds, asset-weighted average). Returns are not guaranteed and real funds vary. No specific fund is recommended. This is not financial advice.
